sections.html:
Hardin County had 113,482 residents in the July 2025 estimate, up 2.5 percent from 2020. Elizabethtown is both the seat and the biggest city, and Fort Knox shapes the local economy. The county has 51,149 housing units, 432 building permits were issued in 2025, and 62.6 percent of homes are occupied by their owners. The market is deep enough that a conference with the assessor can lean on recent sales near your street.

Two school districts matter for a tax bill. Hardin County Schools covers most of the county, and Elizabethtown Independent Schools serves most of the city of Elizabethtown. Each district sets its own rate.

sections.h2: Offices that bill, assess and collect
sections.html:
Everything runs through the government building on North Provident Way in Elizabethtown.

  • Sheriff's Office, tax department: Suite 101, 150 North Provident Way, Elizabethtown, KY 42701. Phone 270-765-5133 and pick option 1.
  • PVA (the assessor): 270-765-2129. Its website has a parcel search, a tax estimator and an exemption page.
  • County Clerk: Suite 103 in the same building, 270-765-2171, open weekdays from 7:45 in the morning to 4:30 in the afternoon. The clerk quotes the payoff on a delinquent prior-year bill.
  • Planning and Development Commission: Suite 225, 270-769-5479, open weekdays from 8 in the morning to 4:30 in the afternoon for building permits outside city limits.

Two cities bill part of the tax themselves. A tax district code of 03 on your bill means the City of Radcliff (270-351-4714), and 06 means the City of Vine Grove (270-877-2422).

The sheriff posted dates for bills due beginning November 1, 2026, which cover the assessment as of January 1, 2026. The discount period is longer than the date written into KRS 134.015.

  • Discount: November 1 through November 30, 2026.
  • Face amount: December 1 through December 31, 2026.
  • 5 percent penalty: January 1 through January 31, 2027.
  • 21 percent penalty: February 1 through April 15, 2027.

A current-year bill has to be paid whole. A single payment can cover several bills when copies are attached, and a stamped, self-addressed envelope brings back a receipt. Paying by card, online or at the counter, adds 2.49 percent. A taxpayer with no bill by early November can call and a duplicate goes out, or print one from the sheriff's tax bill search.

Rates are quoted in cents per $100 of assessed value, and the school district decides which row fits your house.

The totals also include small extension, health and soil lines. City rates for 2026 on real estate are Radcliff 12.9, Vine Grove 16.3, Sonora 20.0, Upton 25.0 and West Point 26.8. Commercial and telecommunication property in the Industrial Taxing District (District 00) carries an extra ten cents under a 2023 ordinance. Timberland Fire Protection charges 2 cents per acre.

The PVA publishes the inspection dates in the News-Enterprise each year and prints them on assessment notices. The window opens the first Monday in May and stays open thirteen days. Hold your conference with the PVA before or during that time.

When the conference settles things, you are finished. When it does not, hand the appeal form to the County Clerk, who sets a hearing before the county board. A further appeal goes to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals.

Collect sale prices from your own neighborhood first. In the Elizabethtown Independent district each dollar of assessed value carries a higher rate, so a successful appeal saves more there than in the county school district.

Owners aged 65 and up, and owners totally disabled, who live in the house can apply at the PVA. The PVA's rate page lists the homestead and disability amount at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, after $46,350 for 2023 and 2024.

That figure comes off the assessed value, so the saving depends on your rate. Questions go to the PVA at 270-765-2129. A buyer has to apply separately after closing, because the exemption belongs to the owner.

sections.h2: Who pays the bill at closing?
sections.html:
The bill is for a calendar year and goes to the person who owned the property on January 1. A closing agent or attorney usually works out each side's share, then either pays the sheriff at the table or gives one party a credit on the settlement statement and leaves the payment to them.

The sheriff will not take a pro-rated payment, so one or both parties must send the full amount. After a transfer, bills normally go in care of the new owner, though a sale near the print date may miss the update. If a bill reaches your old address, forward it to the buyer.

Start with the tax district code on your bill, since it tells you whether the county school rate, the Elizabethtown Independent rate or a city bill applies. Next, confirm with the sheriff that the current year is paid, or agree with the buyer on who will pay it. Call the clerk if any earlier year shows up as delinquent.

If you hold the homestead exemption, tell the PVA about the sale. Make sure the deed lists a mailing address for the new owner's bill. Then ask the closing agent to show the tax split on the settlement statement, so nobody pays the full year twice. A seller who has tax and repair worries at once may find a quick cash sale simpler than a listing, though the payoff still comes out of the proceeds.

The Planning and Development Commission, created by the fiscal court in 1979, serves unincorporated Hardin County, including Glendale, Cecilia, Rineyville, Stephensburg and Colesburg. A building permit application needs an aerial photo of the property showing the structure and its distance from each property line. Sellers who built a deck, shed or addition without a permit can ask the commission's office whether it is on file before a buyer's inspector asks.

Houses inside Elizabethtown, Radcliff and the other cities are handled by those cities' offices.

When April 15 passes, unpaid bills move to the County Clerk. Call 270-765-2171 for the figure. Interest builds monthly, clerk and attorney commissions are added, and the clerk's website carries a delinquent tax calculator and tax sale information.

An owner with back taxes can still close, because the title company pays the certificate out of the proceeds. Owners who would rather skip repairs and a listing can ask a cash buyer for an offer and compare it with the payoff.

faqs.q: What is the discount period on Hardin County bills for 2026?
faqs.a: The sheriff lists November 1 through November 30, 2026. Face amount runs December 1 through 31, and penalties begin in January 2027.

faqs.q: Can I pay a Hardin County bill in installments?
faqs.a: No. Current-year bills cannot be paid in part. One check may cover several bills if a copy of each is attached.

faqs.q: What does a card payment cost in Hardin County?
faqs.a: 2.49 percent of the bill, online or at the sheriff's office. A mailed check to 150 North Provident Way, Suite 101, avoids the fee.

faqs.q: Whom do I call for a payoff on an old Hardin County bill?
faqs.a: The County Clerk at 270-765-2171. Delinquent prior-year bills are held there, and the clerk's website has a calculator.

faqs.q: Which Hardin County cities charge their own tax?
faqs.a: The 2026 schedule lists Elizabethtown, Radcliff, Sonora, Upton, Vine Grove and West Point. For districts 03 and 06 the sheriff points payers to Radcliff and Vine Grove for the separate city bill.
